summary: A0021 records the Owner-directed retirement of exactly four APPROVED P06 contracts: T063 superseded by T105, T064 by T106, T066 by T107 and T067 by T108. The change is four added `superseded_by` fields in todo/config.yaml (T063 -> T105, T064 -> T106, T066 -> T107, T067 -> T108) and nothing else; `git diff` is 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+). Status, attempt, depends_on, task_file, base_commit, candidate_commit, approved_commit and latest_review of the four targets are byte-identical to the base commit 566ae82, and no other config field, task, contract or document was touched. Each successor already declared `replaces`, already depends on the work it replaces, is not itself retired, and names its predecessor in its `## Replacement and migration` section, and the ARCHITECTURE section 2.2 rows landed by A0020 already carry the `superseded by T10x` wording the T005 citation resolver requires. The four open impacts A0013:T063:legacy, A0013:T064:legacy, A0013:T066:legacy and A0013:T067:legacy are resolved; no other impact is closed. Citation, import-graph, acceptance and progress checks are green after the change.
rationale: The four predecessors are exactly the approved P06 contracts that A0014 replaced and whose successors the Owner has now accepted as the current authority for their surfaces. Retirement is the only mechanism the workflow offers for approved work: the contract text, dependencies and approval evidence of the four targets are frozen because each already records what was independently reviewed, so the annotation records the successor without rewriting history or re-reviewing an unchanged deliverable. Every precondition the controller tests before sealing a SUPERSEDE was verified against the candidate config rather than assumed: (1) each successor in `todo/config.yaml` has no `superseded_by` of its own; (2) each successor lists its predecessor in `depends_on` (T105=[T063,T068], T106=[T064,T068,T105], T107=[T065,T066,T068,T105,T106], T108=[T067,T068,T105]) and in `replaces`; (3) each successor contract contains `## Replacement and migration` followed by the predecessor's task token (T105->T063, T106->T064, T107->T066, T108->T067); (4) the only remaining PLANNED consumers of the four predecessors are the four successors themselves, so no ordinary planned task is stranded and no contract repair belongs inside a retirement record; (5) the supersession relation stays acyclic (T063->T105, T064->T106, T066->T107, T067->T108, each terminating) and the dependency graph stays acyclic. The freeze property was measured, not asserted: re-parsing the candidate config, popping only the four `superseded_by` fields, and comparing against the base-commit config yields an identical document, and the only task entries that differ from base are the four targets. `affected_existing_tasks` is empty as a positive finding: the annotation changes no governing document, and every live statement about these four tasks already reads them as history. ARCHITECTURE section 2.2 labels each predecessor row `(predecessor delivery)` and names its successor, and the transition paragraph (docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:171-191) already states that after `superseded_by` the successor is the only current authority. Every PLANNED contract that still mentions a predecessor does so as an explicitly historical or legacy object, measured line by line: T073 (lines 35-36, 54-55, 68: a legacy T063 manifest or T066 lock 'appears, if at all, as an explicitly historical, non-current' artifact), T083 (lines 23, 35, 42: 'A T066 lock stays an immutable historical record'), T084 (lines 48, 65, 75, 83: legacy T063 artifact rendered non-current), T087 (lines 36, 58, 63-65, 73: pre-registry T063 manifest 'never parsed as current'), T088 (lines 44, 67, 71, 79: legacy T063 manifest never treated as current authority), T096 (lines 53-54: predecessor T063/T064/T066/T067 records 'appear only as linked, read-only history'), T102 (lines 60-62, 94-101, 117-119: the unrestricted T064 predecessor surface must not be reached). ADR-003 (lines 73-74) and THREAT_MODEL (lines 369-372, 456-462, 504) likewise treat T063 as predecessor/historical evidence beside the T105 successor. The retirement therefore leaves no existing task asserting something a governing document no longer says, and this record raises no new impact. Nothing in this change touches Intent, Spec, any contract, dependency list, commit identity, evidence pointer or review record, so no collateral document had to change and none did.

impact_assessment.intent: Not applicable and unchanged. No file under docs/intent/ is edited and `intent_revision` stays v1-2026-09-20-backtest-runs-and-permission-entry. The goals the retirement serves are already stated there: G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 requires a registered identity for every strategy that can be backtested, paper-traded or executed, and G-LIVE-GATE-01 keeps promotion gated on reviewed evidence, so pointing the four predecessors at their registry-bound successors implements the recorded Intent instead of amending it. This SUPERSEDE layer may not edit Intent in any case; no Owner decision beyond the supplied direction is needed.
impact_assessment.specification: Not applicable and unchanged. No file under docs/spec/ is edited and `spec_revision` stays v1-2026-09-20-strategy-successor-ownership. The specification side was completed ahead of this record by A0020: docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:119, 120, 122 and 123 read `T063 (superseded by T105)`, `T064 (superseded by T106)`, `T066 (superseded by T107)` and `T067 (superseded by T108)` with `(predecessor delivery)` module annotations, and the four successor rows at lines 155-158 no longer carry a predecessor task token. That wording is exactly what tools/check_citations/resolvers.py:469-485 now demands of a superseded row, and it is present before the field is set, so recording the retirement cannot turn the citation gate red. The transition paragraph at lines 171-191 already states the operational meaning of the annotation: once `superseded_by` records retirement the successor is the only current authority for new writes, evaluation or guidance, and an unapproved successor leaves that current path unavailable and must fail closed rather than fall back to the predecessor.
impact_assessment.contracts: The four target contracts are byte-identical; todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T063.md, T064.md, T066.md and T067.md are not in the diff. Each still states the obligations its review approved, and that is deliberate: a retirement annotation must not rewrite reviewed text, and both the successor and the ARCHITECTURE table carry the current statement of the surface. The four successor contracts were read to confirm they can carry that authority: todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T105.md (replaces T063, `## Replacement and migration` at line 38 names T063 and requires the old `robinhood_lp.reports` publication path via `VALID_STRATEGY_KINDS` to become unreachable), T106.md (replaces T064, section at line 31 names T064 and requires registry-schema validation before any surface is published), T107.md (replaces T066, section at line 31 names T066 and reduces the old lock parser to a read-only legacy reader), T108.md (replaces T067, section at line 35 names T067 and replaces the guide/example as the current authoring entry point). No contract needed or received a text edit.
impact_assessment.dependencies: The retirement preserves every dependency edge and stranding was measured: the only PLANNED tasks whose `depends_on` contains T063, T064, T066 or T067 are T105, T106, T107 and T108, each of which is that predecessor's named successor and therefore the one exempt consumer the controller allows (tools/workflow/core.py:1813-1852 for the seal check and tools/workflow/core.py:871-884 for the activation check). Three APPROVED tasks also consume a predecessor - T064 depends on T063, T065 on T064 and T066 on T064 - and their dependency lists are frozen approval evidence: they are not activatable again, the progress validator raises no issue for an approved consumer, and rewriting them would falsify the reviews of work that has already run, so they are deliberately left untouched. The four successors remain activatable after the annotation because the controller treats the successor of a superseded dependency as satisfied. No dependency was added, removed or re-pointed, and the supersession and dependency graphs were both confirmed acyclic.
impact_assessment.implementation: Not applicable: no file under src/ or tests/ is edited, and no business code, test or fixture changes. The predecessor implementations (`robinhood_lp.reports`, `robinhood_lp.robustness`, `robinhood_lp.experiments` and the T067 authoring guide) remain exactly as approved, because removal or adaptation of a current path belongs to the successor task that owns the cutover, not to an annotation-only retirement; the four successor contracts each require their predecessor's publication path to be unreachable, legacy-reader-only or fail-closed by the time the successor is delivered. The consequence for the Manager is explicit rather than hidden: until T105-T108 are implemented and approved, that surface has no current authoritative write or evaluation path, and no live path may fall back to a predecessor that is now history.
impact_assessment.data: Not applicable in the sense that no data is created, migrated, rewritten or deleted by this amendment. Historical T063 manifests and reports, T064 split/surface/robustness artifacts, T066 locks and search/rejected-run records and the T067 guide remain byte-identical and read-only; the successor contracts require them to stay inspectable legacy artifacts, and forbid backfilling a registry revision they never recorded or presenting them as current promotion evidence. Nothing in this record touches todo/evidence/, todo/reviews/ or the approved_commit identities that anchor those artifacts.
impact_assessment.operations: No runtime, state-machine or tooling change: `python -m tools.workflow validate` returns {"status": "OK"} and the amended config still satisfies todo/schemas/config.schema.json, including the constraint that a superseded task is APPROVED (tools/progress/check.py:297-307). `active_task` stays T067 with `workflow_state` APPROVED, which the controller accepts because the active task's status still matches the recorded state; the retirement does not strand the workflow, because the next activatable task (for example T068, whose dependencies T060/T062/T065 are all APPROVED and none superseded) can still be brought to READY through the ordinary gate, while an amendment is unfinished no activation may start. Operationally the four predecessors move from `Approved` to `Approved (superseded)` in the progress rendering, with the successor named beside each entry.
impact_assessment.security: Not applicable and unchanged. No key material, keystore, password, credential, endpoint, RPC surface, signer surface or environment file is read, printed, copied or edited, and the retirement grants no execution, risk, approval or live authority to anyone: registry and manifest data are non-secret and deterministic, and the successor contracts state explicitly that registry binding confers no execution, approval or promotion authority. The change adds one task identifier per target to a plan-configuration file and touches no permissions.
impact_assessment.verification: Run in this worktree after the edit, each green: `python -m tools.check_citations check --suppressions docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml --config todo/config.yaml` -> 'citation check passed: no findings'; `python -m tools.check_imports check --suppressions docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml --config todo/config.yaml --architecture docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` -> 'import-graph check passed: no findings'; `python -m tools.check_acceptance check --suppressions docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml --config todo/config.yaml` -> 'acceptance check passed: no findings'; `python -m tools.workflow validate` -> {"status": "OK"}. The same three checks were run before the edit and were also green, so the four retirements are what was exercised. `pytest -q` on the worktree gives 2271 passed and 1 skipped once the four forge-dependent modules (tests/test_abi_artifacts.py, tests/test_oracle_drift.py, tests/test_oracle_provenance.py, tests/test_oracle_review_provenance.py) are excluded; those four fail identically with and without this change because `tools/oracle/lib` is a gitignored vendored Solidity dependency that exists only in the main checkout and not in a fresh worktree, which is an environment limitation and not a finding about the retirement. The targeted set tests/test_workflow_contracts.py, tests/test_config.py, tests/test_documentation_citations.py, tests/test_import_graph.py, tests/test_acceptance.py and tests/test_progress.py passes 146 tests. These runs establish that the annotation leaves the repository checks green; they are not acceptance evidence for any task, and the retirement still requires the independent amendment review. The freeze property was verified by comparing the candidate config against the base commit 566ae82 with only the four `superseded_by` fields popped: identical, with exactly the four targets differing from base.
